memos.scout:
Case for buying CODIE now is thin, and I can't make a strong one honestly.

What supports it: the coin is alive at 30 minutes and up 155% over that window. Organic classification, top-3 holder share is low (8.5%), and the top-5 early buyer share is modest (10.8%). Last 15 minutes show real activity: 1,584 buyers, 714 SOL bought, and net positive flow of 44.55 SOL. Buyers outnumber sellers in aggregate and there was no airdrop dump.

What argues against it: the coin is already 32% off its 30-minute high, and last 15 minutes show sell volume (670 SOL) nearly matching buys (714 SOL), with sellers (1,226) far outnumbering the net-flow signal suggests. Sell-to-buy ratio in the first two minutes after graduation was 1.12, and 42% of curve volume came from bundled wallets, a warning sign. The pool is only 140 SOL deep, so a $20 round trip would eat meaningful slippage. Chasing a coin that has already run and is now retracing, with bundle-heavy early flow, fits the pattern that has lost money on recent days.

Verdict: no strong case for buying now. Skip unless fresh data shows the drawdown stabilizing with net inflow turning clearly positive.
memos.skeptic: The most likely loss here is distribution into our buy. The coin is up 155% over 30 minutes but has already pulled back 32% from its high, and the last 15 minutes show heavy selling: sells of 669.85 SOL against buys of 714.4 SOL, with 1,226 sellers out of 1,584 buyers. Net flow is only +44.55 SOL, so buying pressure is fading. The "ORGANIC" label is weak evidence: 42% of curve buys came from bundled wallets, and the completer holds 32% of the curve flow, which points to coordinated early accumulation that can be sold into a late buyer like us. Launch bots were present, and the first two minutes after graduation show a sell-to-buy ratio of 1.12. With a 140 SOL pool, a $20 ticket faces 1.4-5.1% round-trip costs before any move, so the coin needs a sustained bounce just to break even. Given the 20% base-rate loss on random post-graduation buys and this active distribution, I'd skip.
